sentences.en: - President Wright, fellow honorees, deans, very distinguished members of the Board of Trustees and faculty, graduating students, parents and friends.
Yours is a great institution of higher learning, one of the finest in the country.
And your generous decision to make me today one of your honorary graduates is an honor which I deeply appreciate.
And all of you who get your degrees today, congratulations.
Together with you and like you, I know that commencement exercises are more than a ceremony.
They transcend even the rite of passage inherent in their symbolism.
They represent the watershed in your life.
From now on, there will be a before and then after.
You are about to enter the outside world.
Is anyone waiting for you there? And this is the moment you ask yourselves, where am I in my life?
What role has it prepared for me? What is the state of the world out there?
A story which may be useful to the medical graduates, the MDs already.
The story is a man came to his doctor with numerous complaints.
The doctor examines him thoroughly, and at the end, naturally, asks him to open his mouth and said, "Oh friend, I don't like your tongue."
And the patient answered, "That's the only one I have."
Well, graduates, this is the only world we have.
Who or what is there that will tell us what to do in order to preserve our humanity and celebrate that of others?
A future husband or wife, a friend, perhaps a profitable position or situation.
Those who have invested in your education, their talent and knowledge have done so, believing that you will one day emerge in positions of power or influence,
whose decisions may affect the welfare and the lives of many or at least of one other person.
And that will be their reward. So whatever life will take you, whatever your endeavor might be in any field and whatever the social surroundings,
it is what you have received here from your able and inspired teachers that will serve as your vantage points and guides.
Do not forget them. I have not forgotten mine.
Most belong to the distant past. Some were more recent.
All remain in my memory. Isaiah and Rabbi Akiba, Plato and Spinoza, Dostoevsky and Kafka, their vision has retained its haunting quality
and their voice, when I write or when I teach, reverberates in my own.
sentences.zh: 当我写作或教学时，他们的声音会在我自己的声音中回响。

sentences.en: The teacher in me tells you that what he has learned from them is what I can give you: the magic of words and the weight of silence that separates one from the other.
sentences.zh: 我心中的老师告诉你，他从他们身上学到的东西就是我可以给你的：语言的魔力和将彼此分开的沉默的重量。

sentences.en: But I've also learned from others who were their enemies and mine, sad lessons, dark lessons, appalling lessons.
sentences.zh: 但我也从他们的敌人和我的敌人那里学到了悲伤的教训、黑暗的教训、可怕的教训。

sentences.en: They have taught me that education can be frail and culture vulnerable when they are void of moral dimensions.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，如果缺乏道德维度，教育和文化就会变得脆弱。

sentences.en: Whether in the sciences or in the humanities, in the field of law or of religion, your pursuit of knowledge and truth has led you to distinguish between what helps humanity move forward
sentences.zh: 无论是在科学领域还是人文学科，在法律领域还是宗教领域，您对知识和真理的追求使您能够区分什么有助于人类前进

sentences.en: toward light and warmth, and what compels you to remain behind in frustration and darkness.
sentences.zh: 走向光明和温暖，以及是什么迫使你在挫折和黑暗中落后。

sentences.en: I have learned that racism is stupid. Not only is it ugly, it is stupid.
sentences.zh: 我了解到种族主义是愚蠢的。它不仅丑陋，而且愚蠢。

sentences.en: All forms of racism are stupid. As I have learned anti-Semitism was appalling, repulsive, grotesque.
sentences.zh: 所有形式的种族主义都是愚蠢的。据我所知，反犹太主义是令人震惊的、令人厌恶的、怪诞的。

sentences.en: I have witnessed the unspeakable fate of countless Jewish children, the first to be targeted by the enemy for annihilation.
sentences.zh: 我亲眼目睹了无数犹太儿童的难以言喻的命运，他们是第一个成为敌人消灭目标的人。

sentences.en: And when I say the enemy, I do not mean simply the enemy of my people.
sentences.zh: 当我说敌人时，我并不仅仅指我的人民的敌人。

sentences.en: I believe the enemy of one people is the enemy of all people.
sentences.zh: 我相信一个民族的敌人就是全体人民的敌人。

sentences.en: I believe that whatever happens to one community affects all communities.
sentences.zh: 我相信，一个社区发生的任何事情都会影响所有社区。

sentences.en: That is, (everyone applauding) that is why the tragedy of so many children today
sentences.zh: 就是，（大家鼓掌）所以才有了今天这么多孩子的悲剧

sentences.en: moves me so often through frustration and anger.
sentences.zh: 我经常因沮丧和愤怒而感动。

sentences.en: Every minute we spend together, now, my young friends, now somewhere on this planet, a child dies of starvation, disease and violence.
sentences.zh: 我年轻的朋友们，我们在一起度过的每一分钟，在这个星球的某个地方，都有一个孩子死于饥饿、疾病和暴力。

sentences.en: Are we doing enough to save them? Yes, as a Jew, I have learned to view my Jewishness as a fusion between the particular and the universal.
sentences.zh: 我们为拯救他们所做的努力是否足够？是的，作为一名犹太人，我已经学会将我的犹太身份视为特殊与普遍之间的融合。

sentences.en: I have learned to respect those who are not Jewish for what they are and not for what or they are not.
sentences.zh: 我学会了尊重那些非犹太人，因为他们是犹太人，而不是因为他们不是犹太人。

sentences.en: As a Jew, I have learned that even when the Messiah will come, and I believe that as a Jew, that one day redemption must come to humanity, even then the world will not become entirely Jewish.
sentences.zh: 作为一名犹太人，我了解到，即使弥赛亚到来，我也相信，作为一名犹太人，有一天救赎一定会降临到人类身上，即便如此，世界也不会完全变成犹太人。

sentences.en: It'll be boring. (everyone laughing) But it'll be simply more hospitable, caring, and friendlier.
sentences.zh: 会很无聊。 （大家都笑了）但它会更加热情好客、更加关心、更加友好。

sentences.en: I have learned, my young friends, I have learned, I have learned that learning is a passion that must not diminish with years.
sentences.zh: 我已经学会了，我的年轻朋友们，我已经学会了，我已经学会了学习是一种激情，绝不能随着岁月的流逝而减弱。

sentences.en: That applies to memory as well. It needs to be shared lest it remains stifled, icy, silent.
sentences.zh: 这也适用于记忆。它需要被分享，以免它保持窒息、冰冷、沉默。

sentences.en: Memory tells us that past is in the present, even when it is not unraveled.
sentences.zh: 记忆告诉我们，过去就在现在，即使它还没有被解开。

sentences.en: Memory has its own archeology, its own mystery, its own language.
sentences.zh: 记忆有它自己的考古学、它自己的神秘、它自己的语言。

sentences.en: If not complacent or intimidated, it'll enrich your respirations and commitments.
sentences.zh: 如果不是自满或害怕，它会丰富你的呼吸和承诺。

sentences.en: What would culture, education, or indeed civilization be without its lasting and challenging appeal.
sentences.zh: 如果没有持久和具有挑战性的吸引力，文化、教育甚至文明将会是什么样子。

sentences.en: My memory, though, rooted in the darkness of the abyss, has taught me the imperative of solidarity and friendship.
My good friends, when I came place to those places and in those places, people told us then, "Don't think about anyone but yourself.
That is how you will survive." And they were wrong.
Only those who thought of others, anyone who had a friend or a father or a brother, or simply a comrade for whom he or she cares, he or she had a better chance to live
and therefore to survive. My memory had taught me that my humanity is defined by yours.
Even when my fate is different from yours, it is neither superior nor inferior in its authenticity.
Is its name tolerance? No. Tolerance could suggest condescendence.
And I prefer the word respect, which also means respect for your freedom and mine, and for the freedom of those who have no freedom.
I am free not because someone is not, but because he or she is.
And if their freedom is curtailed, mine is blemished.
And that is also true of hope, the most vital element of all human equations.
War is an act of despair. Peace is a song of and for hope.
And my fervent desire has always been to create a hope that is not someone else's nightmare.
Now we have entered just now a new century.
It is still young and so is its hope. But what about its fears? What about its demons?
They are old and so present. Hatred. Religious hatred is still ravaging the human heart in so many places.
Bosnia and Rwanda, all but forgotten, but Somalia and Sudan are not, must not.
In former refugee camps in Yugoslavia, I visited families in the tents, going around from one to the other, from one surviving victim to another
listening to their tales. And not one of them succeeded in completing a story.
They all broke out in tears. And I felt perhaps this is what we must learn to collect tears and turn them into stories,
into gestures of solidarity and compassion.
From my teachers, I also learned the sublime art of questioning.
From Erasmus, I learned to praise folly, and from Montaigne to accept the power of doubt.
I like nature's warning that madness is a consequence, not of uncertainty, but of certainties.
And this we better remember now for that exists a new or renewed scorch name fanaticism that afflicts contemporary events.
In my lifetime, it has already produced collective humiliations and mass murder, political fanaticism in Moscow, and racist fanaticism in Berlin.
Both were defeated, one politically and the other militarily.
But the 21st century is already threatened by a resurrected religious fanaticism of the Middle Ages.
It grows in every religion, even in mine.
And some of its protectionists on the other part, on the other side.
Some call themselves Martys, forgetting that both in Judaism and Christianity, a Marty is someone who dies for God, not someone who kills for God.
So how is one- (everyone applauding) So how is one to fight fanaticism?
Whatever the answer, education must be its principle component.
In conclusion, only this. My young friends, this century is not mine, it is yours.
If there is hope and there must be, you'll shape it and you will justify it.
All I can do is offer you my memories and experiences to help you in your quest so that the years ahead will enable you to confront the inevitable fear and trembling,
which are inherent to the human condition in its fight for better times.
Granted, the world you inherited is far from being safe and peaceful, but it is your task and maybe mine still to improve it.
Remember, one person's courageous humanist initiative or moral commitment can make a difference.
And it has always. One person safe, one person or one family in those dark times, and they remain my idols.
But even then, those who did so distort the honor of the human race and of humanity.
Well, of all Albert Camus sayings, I prefer the one which comes to the denouement of his novel, "The Plague," "When everything is done,"
"After all is said and done," said Camus, "there is more in man," which means in the human being, "to celebrate than to denigrate."
And so today, my young friends, let's celebrate our new beginnings.
Let's celebrate man's power to transcend tragedy and his or her dream to overcome the oppressor's will to conquer and dominate.
Whether you know it or not, in some parts of the planet, there are people who need you and they are waiting for you.
Thank you. (everyone applauding)
